brief: A recognisable, photoreal Flatiron Building (D. H. Burnham, 1902, Renaissance Revival limestone and glazed terracotta) in modern-day New York City: the narrow 22-storey wedge where Broadway meets Fifth Avenue, with today's glass storefronts, the one-storey glass 'cowcatcher' retail annex at the tip, awnings, window AC units, street trees, a lamppost and a subway entrance.
design_notes: Footprint: right-triangle wedge; Fifth Avenue (west) straight north, Broadway (east) at 25 degrees, 22nd Street (south) 85 studs; tip rounded to 6.5 studs. 1 stud ~ 0.28 m.

Three-part composition. Base: ground-floor storefronts between V-jointed rusticated limestone piers, then floors 2-4 fully rusticated with vertical block joints and keystoned windows, capped by a projecting balcony (modillions, corona, balustrade). Shaft: 14 floors of window pairs with pilaster strips, every window framed by jambs, a chamfered hood and a projecting sill that runs on as a string course at every floor; recessed sooted spandrel panels with raised relief; wreath medallions on the piers at two band floors; oriels bulge 1.5 studs on both long sides. Crown: floor 19, then a double-height arcade of round arches on colonnettes with archivolts, keystones and wreaths, under a sooted frieze, dentils, modillion brackets and a 5-stud corona.

Realism comes from materials, bevels and depth: chamfered edges on piers, blocks, sills, hoods and courses; glass recessed ~0.55 studs behind the window surround with dark sash frames and meeting rails; per-block colour variation (limestone/limestone_b, terracotta/terracotta_b); soot finishes on every recessed face under a projection; darker street-level stone.

Material scale: big stone/terracotta tags use the pipeline's seamless tiles (studs_per_tile from the game STYLE.md, 1024 px per tile) so pitting, mottle and rain streaks read at first-person range; cornice and props are uniquely baked so crevice grime shows.

Street today: cowcatcher annex (glass-and-metal, mullion grid, recessed doors, sign band, awnings with valances), recessed storefront doors, sidewalk slabs with gum spots, granite curb, tree pits with trees, a lamppost, and a green subway-entrance railing in the plaza.

Finishes and wear are not in this spec: they come by name from worlds/nyc/STYLE.md and worlds/nyc/areas/flatiron_district/STYLE.md. Tags over the triangle budget are split by height into numbered chunks automatically.
